fact: The national Open Data steering committee (COPIL), meeting at the Agence de Développement du Digital (ADD), debated a 2026 action plan of the government's Open Data programme that includes enriching and maintaining the national open data portal www.data.gov.ma; the document names no open data policy, strategy or law behind the portal and gives no dataset or publisher count.

The Agence de Développement du Digital (ADD) is the organisation publishing a dataset of 1,028 Moroccan startups on data.gov.ma, whose resource was created and last modified on 2025-01-03 (dataset first created 2021-11-16); the document does not say who runs the portal or tie it to an open data policy.

The document shows data.gov.ma operating as a CKAN-based open data portal hosting datasets under an ODbL licence, with ADD as a listed publishing organisation; it does not state who runs the portal or tie it to an open data policy, and gives its date as the 2025-01-03 release.

The portal's own documentation page says the Agence de Developpement du Digital (ADD) manages Morocco's national open data portal and monitors the national Open Data action plan, which the Open Data steering committee (set up December 2019) oversees; no published date, so the page's retrieval date of 2026-08-08 is used.

The ADD's December 2024 operational manual on open data standards says the national open data portal was launched in 2011, that the Agence de Développement du Digital coordinates the Open Data programme and is responsible for the portal, and that every dataset published there must meet its minimum quality criteria; it states that the portal hosts datasets of some administrations and references datasets on sector portals, names no ministry or agency that has released data and gives no dataset or publisher count, and ties the portal to no open data policy, strategy or law.

The Agence de Développement du Digital's data-inventory guide (v1.3, published February 2023, no event date given) refers to a national open data portal on which public bodies publish datasets, with a COPIL Open Data and the ADD setting the common framework; it names no open data policy behind the portal, does not say who runs it, and gives no dataset or publisher count.

The Agence de Développement du Digital's April 2021 manual for Responsables Open Data states that Morocco's national open data portal (data.gov.ma) was launched in 2011, hosts datasets of some administrations and references datasets on sectoral portals; it does not say who runs the portal, ties it to no named open data policy, strategy or law, and gives no dataset or publisher count.

The Agence de Développement du Digital (ADD) launched the new version of the national open data portal on 2021-12-13, in Arabic and French, as part of implementing the Open Data action plan and Morocco's open government commitments.
On the relaunch the ADD reports about 43% more datasets published and 31% more bodies producing open data, giving no absolute counts; the portal gives access to data from several public bodies.
